headline: Wisconsin and sensory creative are still the clearest growth levers, the category is getting more crowded with restaurant-grade and novelty launches, and this week's biggest risk is stale ops data plus a live category quality-control signal from a major recall.

items: Paid efficiency is still strong. Meta delivered $0.13 CPC on 23,828 clicks in the March export, and 'Straight From Wisconsin' remains the standout creative at $0.09 CPC and 5.36% CTR.

Content winners are getting clearer, not fuzzier. YouTube ASMR/texture content led again, with 'Sourdough Frozen Pizza ASMR' at 2,206 views and 118.4% avg view percentage, while relatable everyday TikTok framing still outperformed polished brand copy.
Instagram added 165 followers in-period and reached 234,828 people, with women 35-44 still the clearest organic audience center.

Market validation for Real Dough's lane keeps rising. Katie's, Flour + Water, Di Fara, and Antico all reinforced that restaurant-led, fermentation-forward frozen pizza can win meaningful grocery distribution.

The category got more competitive this week from both ends. Restaurant-authentic brands kept expanding, while incumbents pushed harder into novelty and convenience, including breakfast pizza, microwave crisping trays, stuffed crust, and retailer-exclusive collabs.

A meaningful trust signal hit the category: 25,000+ cases tied to a Bakkavor / Trader Joe's-linked recall were flagged for possible metal contamination. Quality and manufacturing discipline are now part of the marketing story, not just ops.
Meta targeting still skews older than the brand's real community. Paid spend is concentrated in 55+ and 65+, while the organic audience center remains women 35-44.
Operations data is stale and incomplete. The newest ops file is a single Merriment mid-day snapshot from Apr 5, with no fresh current-week operational read across the portfolio.
AGENCY: Keep building Wisconsin/origin and sensory-crust variants. Those are still the most proven paid and organic hooks.
AGENCY: Reduce low-quality conquesting and keep search budget concentrated in branded plus sourdough-intent terms.
AGENCY: Test more 25-44 Meta weighting and judge it on retailer-intent quality, not just cheap clicks from older cohorts.
OPS: Treat quality assurance as a brand asset this week. Be ready with a simple retailer-safe talking point around process discipline and product integrity if recall chatter spreads.
DATA: Fix the stale-dashboard gap before next Friday. Fresh ops snapshots and bounded weekly analytics are the biggest missing inputs right now.

agency_brief.what_worked: Wisconsin/origin messaging, crust-and-texture storytelling, ASMR-style video, and relatable household framing continue to outperform generic premium product creative.
agency_brief.what_didnt: Competitor search remains a weak use of budget, older-skewing Meta delivery is still misaligned with the core community, and polished but non-specific product messaging is not creating the same pull as sensory or founder-rooted content.
agency_brief.recommendation: For the next cycle, stay narrow and sharper, not broader. Prioritize three lanes: (1) more Wisconsin and sourdough-proof creative, (2) more sensory short-form built around crust crackle, bake texture, and cheese pull, and (3) tighter paid targeting toward 25-44 households with stronger store-finder or retail-availability CTAs.
agency_brief.competitive_context: This week reinforced a two-front battle in frozen pizza. On one side, restaurant and chef-backed brands like Katie's, Flour + Water, Di Fara, and Antico are winning with fermentation, authenticity, and clean process stories. On the other, large incumbents are chasing attention with novelty crusts, breakfast occasions, microwave convenience, and co-branded flavor drops. Real Dough is better positioned in the authenticity lane, but it needs that story to stay specific, visible, and operationally credible.

missing: No fresh current-week operations coverage for Third Coast, Flourchild, or Loon Room, and no current-week portfolio-level ops file at all.
This week's analytics synthesis is based on a March-only Whatagraph export, so true week-over-week April performance is not available in the source set.
The review file surfaces sampled reviews and aggregate ratings, but it does not clearly isolate newly posted reviews from this exact week.
stale: Latest operations snapshot is Apr 5 and limited to Merriment Social mid-day only.
Review samples include many older entries, so sentiment should be treated as directional brand signal, not a clean weekly inbox.
anomalies: YouTube average view percentage above 100% still appears to reflect rewatches, not bad math.
Apr 5 Merriment journal-entry imbalance appears to be driven by open tabs in a mid-day snapshot, not necessarily a true close issue.
The Whatagraph source changed reporting windows versus last week's file, so comparisons to prior YTD analyses are directional rather than apples-to-apples.
